**Meridian Tidal Pilot - Final Operations Review Summary**

The critical equipment failure was **Turbine T-4**, which went offline on 14 March 2025 after a corroded bearing seal allowed seawater into the nacelle, causing a multi-week outage. The root cause was corrosion of the bearing seal housing.

Over the 24-month operating period, the pilot delivered **18.7 GWh** to the grid—6% below the 19.9 GWh forecast in the original business case.

The project went significantly over budget: final cost reached **EUR 41.25 million** against an approved EUR 36.7 million, an overrun of EUR 4.55 million (12.4%), driven mainly by the T-4 repair campaign.

On the environmental front, an independent fish-monitoring programme found **no statistically significant change** in fish migration counts after installation (p = 0.41).

Lead engineer Dr. Ines Marchetti recommended replacing the titanium fastener set with duplex stainless steel on all remaining nacelles—a change the steering group accepted in principle.

The final decision: the steering group **approved Phase 2** for Q3 2026, contingent on a completed bearing seal redesign and a successful dry-dock endurance test.
